task_message:
Case L13: segment the lipomatous soft-tissue tumor on this T1-weighted MRI.

Volume: 361x361x266 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.
final_assistant_text:
The case is finished. Summary of what I did:

**Finding the lesion:** After scanning the volume in all three planes, I identified a large (≈80 × 80 × 50 mm), well-circumscribed, homogeneously hypointense mass with a thin bright capsule, located in the intermuscular fat space of the limb. It was the only discrete, space-occupying, encapsulated lesion in the study (other bright structures were marrow-containing bones and normal fat).

**Segmentation:**
- Seeded the model with a single positive point at the mass centre → produced a tight, single-component mask (114.5 mL, extent ax 105–153, cor 143–222, sag 131–213).
- Verified coverage in all three planes (axial/mask zooms, coronal/sagittal through the mask centre), and tested the intensity-based candidates — all of them were thin rims of surrounding bright fat or adjacent muscle, so they were rejected.
- Applied a 2 mm dilation to include the thin bright capsule/rim around the mass, giving the final mask (140.2 mL, 1 component).

**Final review:** the five-slice-per-plane review showed the outline following the lesion in the interior slices and no lesion tissue in the past-the-end slices (just normal anatomy/fat crease), so the mask was saved with medium confidence — the boundary is unambiguous at the mid/lateral levels but slightly ill-defined at the inferior pole, and I could not fully verify the anatomical region from the images alone.
